lastCompletedAction: OF-016 correction loop 1 of 2. The independent review returned CHANGES REQUESTED with one P0, three P1s, five P2s and one process finding; I reproduced every one before accepting it. H-01 (P0) is the serious one and it was my own: 'dismissed as distinct' did not release the payment, it DEAD-LETTERED it. The exclusion I added removed the dismissed counterpart but not the EVENT ITSELF, which sits in `draft` after a release and so is not filtered out of its own candidate set -- on the next pass it scored against itself at 1.0, openDuplicateReview tried to insert financial_event_id = matched_event_id, 0083's distinct_ck rejected it, the pipeline threw on every sweep and the sweeper dead-lettered the payment the reviewer had just released. My own unit test hid it: its mock createDraft minted a fresh event id every call and its candidate list never contained the event under consideration, so it modelled a world the resume path cannot be in. The replacement drives the REAL store and the REAL pipeline across a REAL dismissal. H-02/H-03 (P1): 0087's immutability trigger was `before update or delete` only, so service_role could FABRICATE a resolved review by INSERT (rendering as a real decision by a real named person, with no audit row) and could destroy resolved evidence by TRUNCATE or by cascading a parent delete. Migration 0088 adds an insert boundary, a statement-level truncate guard and a parent-delete guard -- while leaving an OPEN suspicion cascadable, so authorised pre-decision cleanup still works. H-04 (P1): my immutability test could not fail -- a rollback to a savepoint that was never created threw inside a bare catch{}, swallowing the AssertionError; proven inert by reverting the control and watching 17/17 pass. H-05: the AB-BA test gave each reviewer its own review and its other actor used skip locked, so it passed with the lock order inverted; it now has a positive control that deliberately inverts and is asserted to deadlock. H-06: composite (id, company_id) FKs plus a company-joined queue make a cross-company review unwritable rather than merely unrenderable. H-07: three screens gave three answers to the same failed read -- health rendered a reassuring 0 via rows(), approvals silently dropped its banner because supabase-js RETURNS errors rather than throwing; both corrected. H-08: releasing an event whose source had been dead-lettered left a claimable row wearing a terminal stamp. H-09: several documentation claims were false and are corrected, including my '24 database tests' figure -- that was two files, not the package; measured properly, 54 of 58 fail at 0086. H-10 (process): I kept committing evidence work while the review ran, so the tree moved under it; the numbers happened to describe the reviewed SHA but a reviewer could not have reproduced them. The tree now stays frozen at the reviewed SHA until a review returns.

openFindings: OF-016: RESOLVED by migration 0087 (pending independent review). The paused payment now has an authorized, audited, idempotent resolution path and a screen; historic 0083 rows work as they stand.

OF-018 (P2, NOT exploitable, recorded not fixed): `resolve_inbound_review` and `record_inbound_review` (0075) guard with `caller_jwt_role() is distinct from 'service_role'` IN ADDITION to their EXECUTE grant. Fail-closed, so not a hole -- but it contradicts the second half of the rule this package enforces: a genuine service_role caller whose claim text differs (a direct connection sets no GUC) is refused. Cheap to correct; belongs in a bounded follow-up.

OF-017 (P1, INHERENT -- not closed by FOUND-006): under the PostgREST shared-login model every API session authenticates as `authenticator`, which Supabase grants membership of both `authenticated` and `service_role`. SET ROLE is authorised against session_user, so a caller with arbitrary SQL as `authenticated` can `set role service_role` and reach every service-only entrypoint. No in-database control can close this while the login role holds both memberships; it requires a separate connection identity for service work, which is an owner infrastructure decision.

OF-014 residual (P1): a caller with arbitrary SQL as the `authenticated` DB role can forge request.jwt.claims — reading one quotation status per id, and more broadly forging `sub` and so auth.uid(). The unauthenticated half is closed. Belongs to FOUND-006.
